text: Water resource in general is a property of the State, managed by the Government on behalf of the People. All water resources should be managed with peoples trust through local, provincial and national level institutions.
label: State ownership and trusteeship

by the Government on behalf of the People. All water 
resources should be managed with peoples trust through 
local, provincial and national level institutions.

text: Periodically elected Governments should act as the custodian, conservator and a facilitator of all watershed resources on behalf of the State.
label: Government custodial role

sources.sourceText:
2.	 Periodically elected Governments should act as the 
custodian, conservator and a facilitator of all watershed 
resources on behalf of the State.

text: The role of the State should not confined to the welfare of people and conservation of eco-systems aiming present needs but to ensure continuity of such resources for future generations.
label: Intergenerational resource continuity

people and conservation of eco-systems aiming present 
needs but to ensure continuity of such resources for future

text: The Government is obliged to protect, plan, preserve all hydraulic related heritage in the country among other specific roles.
label: Protect hydraulic heritage

sources.sourceText:

text: Establish appropriate policy, legal and institutional frameworks for efficient Integrated Water Resources Management System in place.
label: IWRM frameworks

sources.sourceText:
5.	 Establish appropriate policy, legal and institutional 
frameworks for efficient Integrated Water Resources 
Management System in place.

text: Facilitation on conservation of water resources through multiple stakeholders for optimal utilization of the scarce resource appropriately through scientific approaches while enforcing appropriate regulations for measures on sustainability of water resources infrastructure.
label: Scientific conservation regulation

sources.sourceText:

resource appropriately through scientific approaches

text: Maintain a repository of updated data and information to freely share among relevant stakeholder entities for conservation, development, management and research purposes.
label: Shared water data repository

sources.sourceText:

to freely share among relevant stakeholder entities for 
conservation, development, management and research 
purposes.

text: Facilitate to ensure corporation among stakeholders institutions at local, regional, river basin levels and national level for efficient planning, conservation and management under river classifications for different user classes and classifications through designated committees comprised of relevant stakeholders.
label: Stakeholder coordination committees

sources.sourceText:
8.	 Facilitate to ensure corporation among stakeholders 
institutions at local, regional, river basin levels and national 
level for efficient planning, conservation and management

classifications through designated committees comprised of 
relevant stakeholders.

text: Ensure adequate water for drinking, sanitation, irrigation, environment and social needs at all times.
label: Adequate water for needs

sources.sourceText:
9.	 Ensure adequate water for drinking, sanitation, irrigation, 
environment and social needs at all times.

text: Promote appropriate water efficient irrigation and agri technologies (micro, sprinkler, drip and green house, vertical agriculture etc.) and the efficiency and productivity in all irrigation systems.
label: Efficient irrigation technologies

sources.sourceText:
10.	Promote appropriate water efficient irrigation and agri 
technologies (micro, sprinkler, drip and green house,

text: Transfer appropriate water management responsibilities among stakeholders and user groups based on respective institutional capabilities.
label: Transfer management responsibilities

sources.sourceText:
11.	Transfer appropriate water management responsibilities

institutional capabilities.

text: Support an institutional framework for sound water resources management by facilitating capacity building, legislative instruments and inter-organizational linkages.
label: Institutional capacity framework

sources.sourceText:
12.	Support an institutional framework for sound water 
resources management by facilitating capacity building, 
legislative instruments and inter-organizational linkages.

text: Introduction of national and international best practices on integrated water resources management that are adaptable to local scenarios.
label: Adopt IWRM best practices

sources.sourceText:
13.	Introduction of national and international best practices on 
integrated water resources management that are adaptable 
to local scenarios.

text: Impose penalties for water and watershed polluters and illegal users in accordance with the law, and damage assessment and compensation mechanism should be introduced for polluters.
label: Polluter penalties and compensation

sources.sourceText:
14.	Impose penalties for water and watershed polluters and 
illegal users in accordance with the law, and damage

introduced for polluters.

text: Introduction of an appropriate special fee system for bulk water users and industries.
label: Bulk water user fees

sources.sourceText:
15.	Introduction of an appropriate special fee system for bulk 
water users and industries.

text: Introduction of an appropriate eco-system payment mechanism for hydropower plant operators in the river systems to ensure adequate maintenance of upstream watersheds.
label: Hydropower ecosystem payments

sources.sourceText:
16.	Introduction of an appropriate eco-system payment 
mechanism for hydropower plant operators in the river 
systems to ensure adequate maintenance of upstream

text: Supporting responsible institutions to secure forests and related eco-systems considering the contribution made to protect water catchment areas by forest and associated eco-systems.
label: Protect catchment forests

sources.sourceText:
17. Supporting responsible institutions to secure forests and

systems.

text: Access to Fresh Water is considered as a fundamental human right. Riparian rights, prior rights and customary rights to water will be recognized. Treaty obligations for which the government has been a signatory will be recognized.
label: Water rights recognition

13

text: Appropriate mechanism will be used to regulate large scale water uses for the public wellbeing.
label: Regulate large-scale water use

sources.sourceText:
2.	 Appropriate mechanism will be used to regulate large 
scale water uses for the public wellbeing.

text: Water requirements of wildlife and eco-systems will be identified and ensured.
label: Wildlife and ecosystem water

sources.sourceText:
3.	 Water requirements of wildlife and eco-systems will be

text: Establish baseline data and maintain a repository of data, establish calibrated and validated hydrologic and hydraulic models of watersheds and water resources on scientific basis for decisions on water quantity and quality, and incorporate the trans basin concept into water resources planning and management appropriately.
label: Data and planning models

sources.sourceText:
1.	 Systematic and provident planning system is essential for 
efficient water resources management to avoid unnecessary 
spending and to avoid hydrological disasters. Hence, 
establishing baseline data and maintaining a repository of 
data is highly essential. Establish calibrated and validated 
hydrologic and hydraulic models of watersheds and water 
resources on scientific basis for all decisions on water quantity 
and quality. Trans basin concept shall be incorporated into 
water resources planning and management appropriately.

text: Water resources planning for national and provincial development should include review of existing plans, set out national policies, appropriate regulations and standards, improved water resources development plans, and aesthetic, heritage (archaeological) and natural values.
label: National-provincial planning framework

sources.sourceText:
2.	 Water Resources Planning for national and provincial 
development should include review of existing plans, set 
out national policies, appropriate regulations and standards 
improved water resources development plans; aesthetic, 
heritage (archaeological) and natural values.

text: Water resources conservation, development and management plans should be prepared for all major river basins, smaller basins, sub basins and cascade systems, with multi stakeholder participation, considering agriculture, drinking, ecological, industrial, power generation and recreational requirements, and aiming for self-sustainability in conserving and managing optimum water resources within schemes, river basin or aquifer, Province and Nation.
label: Basin plans with participation

sources.sourceText:
3.	 Water 
resources 
conservation, 
development 
and 
management plans should be prepared for all major river 
basins, smaller basins, sub basins and cascade systems. Plans 
shall be prepared with a multi stakeholder participation. 
(Ex- Design of dams considering, agriculture, drinking, 
ecological, industrial, power generation, recreational 
requirements. Attempts should to be taken to ensure self-
sustainability in conserving and managing optimum water 
resources within the schemes, within river basin or aquifer, 
within the Province and ultimately within the Nation.
